comparison: Both evaluations strongly support the finding that RBBP6 depletion selectively affects sense but not antisense transcription. OpenEval cites converging experimental evidence from POINT-seq (C27-C36), while peer reviewers explicitly confirm 'depletion of the required CPA factor RBBP6 has little effect on antisense transcription' and praise the methodology as rigorous. Complete agreement on this finding.

Both evaluations unanimously support INTS11's preferential effect on antisense transcription (C39-C47). OpenEval describes 'comprehensive POINT-seq evidence' while peer reviewers call the work 'excellent' with 'very good' data quality. Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly confirms 'depletion of Integrator endoribonuclease INTS11 leads to globally increased transcription in the antisense direction.' Complete agreement.

Both evaluations strongly support the novel sPOINT-seq methodology and finding of preferential sense initiation (C4, C48-C52, C89, C116). OpenEval notes the data is 'well-supported' while peer reviewers highlight this as a major technical advance that 'can positively impact work in the field.' Both recognize the novelty and quality of this contribution.

Both address the interpretation that INTS11 effects are not due to increased initiation (C53-C54). OpenEval finds this 'logically sound' based on sPOINT data, while peer reviewers accept this interpretation as consistent with the overall model that INTS11 affects elongation/termination. Agreement on this mechanistic interpretation.

Both evaluations strongly support the central finding that CDK9 inhibition sensitizes sense transcription to INTS11 (C5-C7, C62-C69, C88, C117). OpenEval describes 'strong POINT-seq evidence' while peer reviewers call the experimental design 'elegant' and evidence 'compelling.' Both accept the conclusion that CDK9 protects sense transcription from INTS11. Complete agreement.

Both evaluations support the HIV reporter experiments demonstrating CDK9 recruitment alleviates INTS11-dependent attenuation (C8, C80-C87). OpenEval describes this as an 'orthogonal approach' strengthening the main findings, while peer reviewers accept it as part of the 'elegant experimental design' without objection. Agreement on this supporting evidence.

Both evaluations support the western blot data showing phosphorylation patterns (C73-C75). OpenEval notes the data is supported but finds the mechanistic interpretation about redundant kinases (C76) speculative. Peer reviewers accept the biochemical data as part of the overall 'very good' data quality without specific challenge. Agreement on data, with OpenEval more cautious about mechanism.

Both evaluations support the CDK7 inhibition data (C77) but recognize the mechanistic explanations (C78-C79) as speculative. OpenEval states 'the mechanism remains uncertain' while peer reviewers accept it as 'supporting rather than definitive evidence.' Both appropriately acknowledge this as a supporting observation requiring further investigation. Agreement on evidentiary status.

Both evaluations support the observation of CDK9-sensitive antisense transcription and 5' recovery (C70-C72). OpenEval notes this represents 'a nuance to the main model' showing effects are 'not strictly binary,' while peer reviewers accept this complexity as consistent with biological reality without undermining main conclusions. Agreement that this adds complexity without contradicting the model.

Both evaluations recognize the hypothesis about promoter element arrangement (C90, C94) as speculative. OpenEval states 'the mechanistic explanation requires further investigation' while peer reviewers explicitly note 'the bias in transcriptional initiation directionality remains to be elucidated' as a weakness. Agreement that this is an untested hypothesis requiring future work.

Both evaluations address the speculation about INTS11 endonuclease activity and association mechanisms (C95-C97, C100). OpenEval notes the hypothesis 'remains speculative' with important methodological caveats, while peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate these molecular details, focusing instead on functional findings. Both implicitly accept these as reasonable but untested hypotheses.

Both evaluations address mechanistic hypotheses about SPT5 phosphorylation and INTS11 association (C98-C102, C100). OpenEval rates this as UNCERTAIN, stating the mechanism is 'speculative and not directly tested,' while peer reviewers acknowledge these are hypotheses not explicitly evaluated. Agreement that these represent plausible but unproven mechanisms.

Both evaluations address speculation about INTS11-independent attenuation and exosome targeting (C103-C107, C106). OpenEval notes this 'relies partly on prior literature' rather than direct experimental evidence, while peer reviewers accept this observation as part of overall findings acknowledging biological complexity. Agreement that this is interpretive rather than directly demonstrated.

Both evaluations address the overall model synthesizing findings (C116-C121, C62-C63). OpenEval finds the model 'well-supported by convergent evidence,' while peer reviewers note a limitation: residual sense bias when both INTS11 is degraded and CDK9 inhibited suggests 'other unknown factors.' OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED; peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN due to incomplete explanation. Partial disagreement on completeness of model.

OpenEval evaluates claims about different termination complexes targeting different RNAPII forms (C108-C112), finding them supported by citations and consistent with experimental data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual/discussion claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims about U1 sites and Integrator/Restrictor sensitivity (C113-C115), finding them appropriately supported by citations to recent literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these discussion/contextualization claims.

OpenEval evaluates background claims about bidirectional transcription and evolutionary conservation (C1-C3, C9-C13), finding them well-established and appropriately cited. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/introduction claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims describing the prior model for promoter directionality (C14-C17), finding them accurately represent published literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims establishing conceptual framework.

OpenEval evaluates claims about Integrator complex composition and function (C18-C24), finding them accurately describe established knowledge with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims about temporal and spatial dynamics of INTS11 and CDK9 (C56-C61), finding them well-supported by multiple citations providing mechanistic context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature-based contextual claims.
